decision.owner: Repository owner Yes on the narrow contract-evolution policy amendment, 2026-10-15; applied here by the coordinator after independent review
decision.reference: Authorization bead bu-vcwgbn for implementation bead bu-gm93xc (PR #4666, the central fact writer refuses writes against merge-tombstoned entities). Reviewed before: main 5ea5bd4d95667361e0b4c914a61f71fccd3a4e3e plus the REQ-relationship-facts-002 header lines this change adds; approved subject: PR #4666 head ebc004e65929c355fa97ff5f525f0af52c788d7a (review bu-f9dwbf), merged with that main plus the request file. Governing requirement REQ-relationship-facts-002 (Central writer — relationship_assert_fact()) of openspec/specs/relationship-facts/spec.md, whose pre-change block carried no ID and gains it in this change, byte-identical to the header the open change relationship-fact-effective-time already carries in its MODIFIED copy. One owner changes assertions to the typed refusal; the other eight (every test in roster/relationship/tests/test_resolve_outbound_channel.py) are fixture-context only: their bodies are byte-identical and only the module's hand-rolled public.entities stub gains the nullable metadata JSONB column the production table already has, because the writer now reads it. This exact manifest requires its own independent review and protected-main publication before consumption; provenance text grants no runtime admission.

owners.reason: The removed assertions pinned the known gap (bu-gm93xc): a write queued behind a committing merge inserted onto the tombstoned source. REQ-relationship-facts-002 now requires the writer to refuse it with entity_tombstoned naming the survivor. The test keeps its lock-order intent (the writer queues on public.entities and the merge moves the original row intact) and now asserts the typed refusal, the survivor id and nothing active on the source.

Fixture context only. The module's pool fixture adds a nullable metadata JSONB column to its hand-rolled public.entities stub, matching the production table, because REQ-relationship-facts-002's tombstone refusal makes the central writer read public.entities.metadata on every write. No assertion, test body or other helper changed; without the column the five tests that reach the writer fail with UndefinedColumnError, and the other three are unaffected.
